paragraphs.source_en: You could pack up the family in a camper and travel around the country. You could strap on a backpack and tour the world. You could read. You could do every household project on your list. You could learn a new trade. You could explore your creative side, painting pictures or making music for the sheer pleasure of it. You could spend the whole year in a systematic job search for the work that suits you to a T. You could get your GED, BA, or MA and qualify for a whole new level in your chosen field of work. You could volunteer full-time for a cause you care about and maybe even be asked to stay on as paid staff. You could get reacquainted with your family.

paragraphs.source_en: Try this: Ask yourself how you would spend your time if you could take a year off with pay. Don’t be surprised if you find your mind a total blank; complete identification with your job may have temporarily suppressed your true dreams and desires. But stay with the question and discover the possibilities of what you would choose to do if you had enough savings that you didn’t need paid employment for one year.

paragraphs.source_en: How do you feel about having savings? What are your thoughts about it—for or against? Are you postponing it, thinking you’ll do it later or when you’ve paid off your debt or when you have a better job? Does having savings compromise your self-image? Does it represent the passage of your youth or capitulation to your parents? Is it something that you’ll get around to “one day”? Are you a spendthrift who thinks the term “disposable income” means you get to spend every last penny in your pocket? Does saving seem like an impossible dream, given your current financial status? What about your religious or political convictions about saving money? Should you be tithing your excess money to the church, giving it to the poor, or donating it to a cause?
